headline: High risk of prompt injection and data leakage if agentic-flow feeds Notion AI workspace content or MCP outputs into its workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can use MCP, stdin/stdout, and background workers, so it can ingest external content; agent_b is a workspace Q&A system over pages/databases. If agent_a routes Notion content or MCP output into prompts, agent_b may treat attacker-controlled text as trusted instructions. The shared channel is plausible, but not directly documented, so uncertainty stays medium.
conditions: IF agent_a ingests Notion page text or MCP output into prompts without provenance filtering, injection is possible.
IF agent_b returns workspace content that agent_a later parses as instructions, the pathway is active.
mitigations: Add a strict instruction/data delimiter in agent_a prompts.
Strip or neutralize imperative text before passing Notion content onward.
Require provenance tags on all MCP-fed content.
Review one representative workflow for prompt concatenation.
requires-engineering: add allowlist-based prompt parsing.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b can access workspace pages and databases under the user's Notion permissions, while agent_a touches code, repository metadata, and task prompts and can use network egress/MCP. If agent_a sends workspace content or repo data into vendor backends, sensitive material can leave the workspace boundary. The pairwise leakage path is plausible from the profiles, though not directly observed.
conditions: IF agent_a forwards Notion workspace text into external APIs, leakage occurs.
IF agent_b surfaces confidential workspace pages that agent_a stores or transmits, cross-system exposure occurs.
mitigations: Limit agent_a inputs to redacted excerpts.
Disable sharing of full page exports from Notion to agent_a.
Check one workflow for secrets or PII before transfer.
Use separate workspaces for sensitive and non-sensitive content.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before any handoff.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can modify git state and run shell commands, while agent_b cannot write filesystems or modify git state. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only overlap is indirect workspace content handling, so this is a limited coordination risk rather than a true capability collision.
conditions: IF agent_b is extended with write access to the same repository, conflict risk rises.
IF agent_a and agent_b are both pointed at the same mutable git checkout, contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep agent_b read-only for repository-adjacent tasks.
Avoid using agent_a on the same checkout during Notion syncs.
Document a single writer for git state.
Check whether any automation writes back from Notion to repo.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, so it may present retrieved text as authoritative. agent_a can then use those outputs in downstream analysis or automation via shell/MCP. Without an explicit verification step, errors from agent_b can cascade into agent_a actions, but the profiles do not show irreversible action authority by default.
conditions: IF agent_a consumes agent_b answers as facts without verification, cascading error is active.
IF agent_a uses those answers to generate repo changes or reports, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Require source links for every Notion-derived claim.
Add a human review step before agent_a acts on agent_b output.
Compare agent_b answers against original workspace pages.
Limit agent_a to draft-only outputs.
requires-engineering: implement citation validation.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b is vendor-hosted and uses Notion workspace permissions, while agent_a is open-source and can handle Ed25519 signatures and repository metadata. The profiles do not show PHI, EU-only data, or a residency mismatch, so only a modest compliance gap is evident: different hosting and retention regimes may apply to workspace content versus local repo data.
conditions: IF PHI or regulated data is placed into Notion pages, compliance review is required.
IF the workspace contains jurisdiction-restricted data, vendor-hosted processing may become noncompliant.
mitigations: Classify data before placing it in Notion.
Keep regulated data out of agent_b workspaces.
Confirm retention settings for the workspace.
Separate sensitive and general-purpose projects.
requires-engineering: document a DPA and residency review.
